newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian residential property in favour-survey.
newsitem.headline: Australian residential property in favour-survey.

text.p: Australian property investors have a shown a strong shift in preference for floating rate loans, and see residential property as the best investment in the sector, the Ashe Morgan Winthrop survey has found.
Expectations for the property sector were varied across states with New South Wales (NSW) and Victoria more optimistic than other states.

"The survey's first significant finding was the differing attitudes towards funding options, with institutional borrowers more optimistic in their outlook for a further interest rate easing than residential investors," Ashe Morgan Winthrop group
The survey found that 46 percent of respondents would opt for floating rates if they were to borrow money in the next three months, up from 29.4 percent a year ago.
This was still below the 50 percent preference level for fixed rate loans, but this had dropped 11.6 percentage points over the past year.
Retail, commercial and industrial investors favoured floating rate finance, while residential borrowers were favouring fixed rate funding, the survey found.

Ashe Morgan Winthrop said in a statement issued with the survey results that it was Australia's leading commercial mortgage originator and the only originator established solely to serve the property industry.

The semi-annual survey, covering more than 400 professionals including property investors, lending staff, property consultants and property advisers, also found a significant difference in attitudes in different states on the outlook for the economy and property market.
"Expectations were particularly high in New South Wales and Victoria, while the majority of Queensland respondents were uncertain or negative about the future," Moss said.

Residential property was the favoured sector of investment for 38.5 percent of respondents, a 33 percent increase since December 1996. In New South Wales, 49.1 percent of respondents favoured residential property.
Against this, sector specific investors still favoured their own sector for investment over residential.
The residential sector is expected to continue to boom, the survey said, with 61.5 percent expecting the market to improve over the next three months and only one percent expecting it to worsen.
The survey found 29.6 percent of respondents thought the current housing upturn would last two, three or more years, while 24.7 believed it would last for the next six to 12 months.
Residential borrowers were most optimistic on the length of the upturn.

When choosing a type of lending institution, 39.2 percent of respondents nominated non-bank institutions, with 22.7 percent favouring banks. The preference for using banks has fallen by 31 percent in the last six months, the survey said.
A further 34 percent said the decision was not one of simply choosing either a non-bank or bank.

"Borrowers indicated that factors such as price, fees and charges, level of service, security, flexibility and terms and conditions are influencing their decision in source of funds," the survey report said.
